ios.desc:
Most projects stall not because you lack motivation — but because "finish the project" is too vague to ever act on. You open a blank to-do list, dump in a dozen tasks, and within a week it's either abandoned or buried under newer ones.

Milestones is built around a different idea: every project deserves structure, and structure is what makes finishing possible.


A smarter way to plan
Milestones introduces a three-tier hierarchy — Projects, Milestones, and Tasks — that mirrors how real work actually happens. A project isn't one thing; it's a series of phases. Each phase has its own focus, its own deadline, its own definition of done. Milestones makes that structure explicit so you always know where you are and what's next.


Break goals into phases
Every project is divided into named milestones — the chapters of your work. Whether you're building an app, writing a thesis, planning an event, or launching a side project, milestones give you a natural way to chunk the journey into stages you can actually complete one at a time.


Track progress visually
Each milestone has its own live progress bar showing task counts and completion percentage. At a glance, you can see how much you've done, how much is left, and which phases are moving. No more guessing whether you're close or far.


Focus on what matters right now
Mark one milestone as Active. It pins to the top of your project, pulses with a live indicator, and becomes your single point of focus. Everything else stays visible but secondary — giving you clarity without losing context.


Organized from every angle
Milestone statuses — Draft, Planning, In Progress, In Review, Released — give each phase a clear stage in the lifecycle. Tasks are sorted into To Do, In Progress, and Done sections automatically. Tag tasks to group related work across a project. Store unscheduled ideas in the project backlog so nothing falls through the cracks.


Designed to look as good as it works
Give every project its own icon — choose from a curated set of symbols or use your own photo — paired with a custom color. Your project list becomes a visual dashboard that's satisfying to open every day.


Manage projects with AI
Milestones includes a built-in MCP server — connect Claude and other AI agents on your Mac to create projects, add tasks and move milestones forward just by asking. Your project planner, now AI-native.

quotes.text:
Hello HN!

I got pretty overwhelmed with Notion, Trello, etc. (Even though they are great tools!) as an indie dev, so I built an app that is simpler to use and perfectly suited for an indie like me :)
You can basically divide your projects into multiple milestones (a milestone could be e.g. a new version), and the milestones can have multiple tasks that are either todo, in progress, or done. The progress for each milestone is calculated with those tasks, and you can also prioritize and categorize the tasks using tags (E.g. for me, #ph turns into "High Priority", and #pm into "Medium Priority", etc.).
Each project also has a backlog for future tasks & ideas, and I'm also currently working on adding markdown-based project notes to describe more complex ideas.

I built this tool for myself (and I'm actively using it), and thought it would benefit others as well.

I'd love to hear feedback and your thoughts! :)

quotes.text:
Hello HN!

I wanted to show you the project management app that I've been building for the past 2 years: Milestones! It's completely native and works on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

It doesn't need an account, it's local-first, with optional iCloud Sync that can be turned on in settings. iCloud Sync means that your data can be synced but still stays private, as it syncs to your own iCloud account. Additionally, analytics and crash reports are opt-in and you're asked before any data is sent to any analytics server.

I built this app for myself, since I am handling multiple projects constantly, but wanted a way to manage them without having to use bloated, complex tools, plus I needed a way to divide tasks into "phases" or milestones (e.g. App versions).

It's free to download and has a generous free-tier, the pro version comes with a monthly, yearly or lifetime option and is mainly for power-users. I also just released an MCP Server for the Mac version.

I'd love for you all to try it and tell me what you think, I'm very open to feedback, critics, and suggestions!

You can get it on the [iOS App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/project-planner-milestones/id6737195092), and the [Mac App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/project-planner-milestones/id6737195092?platform=mac), or you can take a look at the [website](https://getmilestones.app/) first (though to be honest some of the screenshots and info on the website are already outdated)
